Hi Grace —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are moving toward a Dedicated capacity evaluation and need to land on the regional capacity sourcing + burst policy before the procurement doc is finalized. High level:

- Workload: real-time assistant + nightly batch analytics (inference + embeddings).
- Peak tokens/sec (inference): ~1,200 tokens/sec global with a 3x burst window (~3,600 t/s) for promotional spikes.
- Region preference: primary us-west1, but we need EU fallback (eu-west1) for GDPR traffic; APAC not critical for initial phase.
- Compliance: SOC2 attestation required (we attached a summary); we will also run an internal security review.

Questions we need answers to before procurement:
1) Can Redwood commit to a primary/secondary region pairing with automated fallback?
2) What initial pool size and GPU types would you recommend for the mix (low-latency inference + batch embedding jobs)?
3) How does autoscale + burst work: warm pools, cold-starts, cost/credit mechanics when bursting to a larger pool?
4) Expected latency SLOs and regional replication lead times for failover?

I've attached a simple traffic profile (novacorp_traffic_profile_q3.csv) and SOC2_summary_redacted.pdf.

Can we schedule a 30-minute intake call this Friday to lock the decision matrix and list the procurement deliverables? Preferred times: 10:00–11:30 PT or 14:00–16:00 PT.

Thanks —

Alice — great context, thanks for the traffic file and SOC2 snapshot. We'll run intake on the data and come prepared with a recommendation and a decision checklist for procurement. Quick answers up front so your team can triage: 

1) Primary/secondary pairing: yes — Redwood supports automated regional fallback. We recommend active-primary in us-west1 with active-passive (replicated KV cache + warm standby) in eu-west1 for GDPR flows. Failover is automated by routing policy; options for immediate failover or a staged cutover.

2) Initial pool size & GPU choice: based on the traffic sample and mixed workload, our preliminary suggestion is a dedicated pool sized for sustained baseline of ~4 x H100-equivalent GPUs (inference-optimized) with an additional 6-GPU burst budget available across the region pair. H100 gives best latency for generative and dense-embedding workloads; we can propose an A100 mix if budget is constrained.

3) Autoscale & burst model: Redwood offers a two-tier approach — scale-up autoscaling for sustained increased throughput (policy-driven), and a burst buffer for short windows (minutes to hours) that can pre-warm instances. Bursts incur additional usage over committed capacity and are billed per-minute; we can provide an example credit schedule in the procurement appendix. Warm standby reduces cold-start risk for burst.

4) Latency SLOs and failover: Typical 95/99 P90 latencies for this class with H100 are 60–120ms / 180–300ms depending on prompt length and batching. Failover replication of prefix/KV cache is best-effort and we estimate 30–90s for route-level failover; for stronger consistency we can do session pinning per region but that impacts failover seamlessness.

Action items for Friday intake (30m):
- Confirm regions and regulatory constraints (Alice + procurement)
- Validate target SLOs and cost envelope (Ben + Priya)
- Technical acceptance criteria and prep list for security review (Priyom)

I'm free Friday 10:30 PT. If that works for you we'll send a calendar invite and a short intake agenda.

Thanks —

Thanks — adding a technical checklist from implementation: 

- Workload characterization: we'll need a representative prompt set (short/medium/long) and embedding batch size distribution. The CSV helps but we'll ask for a 1-hour sample trace if possible.
- KV cache sizing: estimate ~8–12GB KV per active model for prompt caching; if you have session affinity we can budget per-region caches.
- Prefix caching + routing: recommend global routing with per-region affinity and an ordered fallback (us-west1 -> eu-west1).
- Autoscale policy: start with CPU/GPU utilization triggers at 65% (scale up) / 30% (scale down) with a minimum cushion of 10% reserved for latency headroom. Burst policy: pre-warm policy that starts instances when predicted traffic crosses a 2x sustained baseline for 2 consecutive minutes.
- Quantization/Model profile: we'll publish a recommended quantized variant for embedding workloads to reduce burst cost — we can validate quality on your eval prompts.

Deliverables for intake:
1) Confirmed call time + attendee list.
2) 1-hour trace (UTC timestamps) and sample prompts.
3) Procurement constraints (hard caps, billing contacts).
4) Security assessment lead and required artifacts list.

I'll prep an ops-runbook draft and a minimal acceptance test checklist to share post-call.

—Priyom
